issues.description: No application-level rate limiting anywhere on login, register, or password-reset endpoints. Brute-force/credential-stuffing protection depends on GoTrue's own built-in per-IP rate limiter, which requires GOTRUE_RATE_LIMIT_HEADER to identify real client IPs behind Kong. As of commit 7080d4e, docker/docker-compose.yml sets GOTRUE_RATE_LIMIT_HEADER=X-Forwarded-For for the auth service — a real, directionally-correct improvement for non-adversarial traffic. However, docker/kong.yml has no ip-restriction plugin and neither compose file nor kong.yml configures KONG_TRUSTED_IPS/real_ip_header, so Kong does not strip/replace a client-supplied X-Forwarded-For before appending its own hop (standard nginx proxy_add_x_forwarded_for behavior: append, not replace). GoTrue reads the leftmost entry of X-Forwarded-For as the rate-limit key (per Supabase's own documented guidance that the header must be set by a trusted proxy). On the Docker self-host deploy target (Kong's proxy port exposed directly to the internet, no intermediate trusted proxy), a client can send its own X-Forwarded-For before ever reaching Kong and vary it per request to defeat per-IP rate limiting entirely. Not a regression (pre-fix, GoTrue had no way to distinguish clients behind Kong at all), but the fix does not fully close the gap against a deliberate attacker as its commit message implies.
evidence: docker/docker-compose.yml (kong service: no KONG_TRUSTED_IPS/real_ip_header; auth service: new GOTRUE_RATE_LIMIT_HEADER: X-Forwarded-For line)
docker/kong.yml (2 services, only `cors` plugin on each, no ip-restriction/rate-limiting/trusted-proxy config)
WebSearch: Kong docs on trusted_ips/real_ip_header being required for Kong to treat upstream IP headers as authoritative
WebSearch: Supabase/GoTrue rate-limit docs stating the rate-limit header 'is expected to be set by a trusted upstream proxy' and is otherwise spoofable

history.note: Independently confirmed still absent; not a new finding, first time tracked under a REL-* ID.

Commit 7080d4e added GOTRUE_RATE_LIMIT_HEADER=X-Forwarded-For, a real improvement for honest traffic, but independently found (via WebSearch on Kong's and GoTrue's real forwarding/parsing behavior, since neither is vendored in this repo) that Kong's default config in this stack does not sanitize a client-supplied X-Forwarded-For before appending its own hop, and GoTrue trusts the leftmost (client-controlled) entry — so a deliberate attacker on the Docker self-host deploy target can still bypass per-IP rate limiting by spoofing the header. Status stays OPEN, not VERIFIED; the fix is a real partial improvement, not a closure of the finding as its commit message claims.

issues.description: `npx create-kontrolia-auth migrate` and `update` used to apply pending migrations directly against whatever Postgres connection string the user pastes into a plain text prompt, with zero confirmation, dry-run, or backup step. As of commit 7080d4e, packages/cli/src/index.ts's runMigrateCommand and runUpdateCommand now parse the connection string's host via connectionHost()/isLocalHost() and, for a URL-format string with a non-local host, show a p.confirm() naming the host before proceeding — genuinely closes the original gap for the documented connection-string format. `install`'s own auto-provision path intentionally was not given this gate (different risk profile: a first-time setup where the user is deliberately choosing a fresh target, not re-applying against a possibly-live database) — consistent with the original finding's own framing. Two new, narrower gaps surfaced by this investigation are tracked separately: REL-DEPLOY-003 (grant-admin has no gate at all) and REL-DEPLOY-004 (the host-parsing fails open — treated as local — for non-URL connection-string formats).
evidence: live node -e test of connectionHost()/isLocalHost() against 6 real connection-string shapes

issues.description: packages/cli/src/index.ts's connectionHost() (added by commit 7080d4e) parses the pasted connection string with `new URL()`. Live-tested against the libpq keyword/value connection-string format (`host=... port=... dbname=... user=... password=...`), a real and commonly-used Postgres connection-string shape that `psql` and some tools accept: parsing throws, connectionHost() catches it and returns null, and isLocalHost(null) is defined to return true — so an unparseable string is silently treated as local and the confirmation prompt is skipped entirely, applying migrations straight away. The code's own comment candidly documents this exact fail-open tradeoff ('an unparseable string just skips the localhost check and confirms anyway'), so it's a known, accepted design choice by the author, not a hidden defect — but it does undermine the safety net for any operator who pastes a non-URL-format connection string, which the free-text p.text() prompt does nothing to prevent.
evidence: packages/cli/src/index.ts:15-22 (connectionHost, with its own comment acknowledging the fail-open behavior)
live node -e test: 'host=prod-db.example.com port=5432 dbname=mydb user=x password=y' => host: null, isLocal: true

issues.description: No external call in the backend (GoTrue admin API calls in findUserByEmail, callGotrueAdmin, resolveEmails()'s admin.auth.admin.listUsers() loop) has an explicit timeout/AbortController. A hung or slow GoTrue instance would hang the route handler indefinitely, bounded only by the hosting platform's own request timeout. As of commit 7080d4e, findUserByEmail (platform-admins/route.ts) and callGotrueAdmin (oauth-clients/route.ts) — both raw fetch() calls — genuinely gained AbortSignal.timeout(10_000), and findUserByEmail also gained a try/catch it was missing entirely (real, independent fix). However, resolveEmails()'s admin.auth.admin.listUsers() calls in BOTH organization-members/route.ts and platform-admins/route.ts go through the Supabase JS SDK client (createSupabaseAdminClient(), apps/auth-server/lib/supabase-admin.ts) rather than a raw fetch() — that client has no custom fetch/timeout override configured anywhere, so these two call sites (which back the actual Users list and Platform Admins list pages, arguably the highest-traffic admin-panel screens) remain completely unbounded. The commit's claim of covering 'every GoTrue admin API call' is not accurate.
evidence: apps/auth-server/app/api/platform-admins/route.ts:43-53 (findUserByEmail, now has timeout+try/catch) and :77-97 (resolveEmails, still unbounded)

history.note: Not blocking at current self-hosted scale; worth a follow-up before scaling to untrusted/high-latency deployments.

Partially fixed, not VERIFIED. Commit 7080d4e's diff read line-by-line: the 2 raw fetch() call sites (findUserByEmail, callGotrueAdmin) genuinely gained AbortSignal.timeout(10s). But resolveEmails()'s SDK-mediated listUsers() calls — explicitly named in this issue's original description — were not touched at all; createSupabaseAdminClient() has no timeout configured. Status stays OPEN with a corrected, narrower description; not the full closure the commit message claims.

issues.description: Migrations 0028-0030 change previously-permitted (but insecure) write behavior to now be rejected (blocking membership.user_id reassignment, requiring an existing Owner to grant Owner, blocking role slug hijacking). Under strict semver this is arguably 'minor' (breaking behavior change for any consumer relying on the old permissive behavior), but all 7 changesets for @kontrolia/db are tagged 'patch'. Shipping security-hardening fixes as patch is standard industry convention (same as CVE-fix versioning) and is defensible, not a defect — flagged as a release-notes consideration, not a blocking issue.
